findings.current: If my life was enough to put an end to that, I’d count myself lucky.
findings.defect: The Korean says it would be fortunate if he could settle the cost with his life alone; it does not say his death would put an end to Dark Heaven’s actions.
findings.rationale: “퉁칠 수 있다면” expresses settling or making up for the losses with one person, not necessarily ending the cause of those losses.
findings.replacement: If I could settle the score with my life alone, I’d count myself lucky.

findings.current: countless people had gone to their deaths on the execution grounds
findings.defect: This drops the source’s execution-ground dew image, which the accepted baseline preserved.
findings.rationale: The Korean uses the image “형장의 이슬로 사라졌어도” (“vanished as dew on the execution grounds”); the current line conveys the deaths but omits that image.
findings.replacement: countless people had vanished like dew on the execution grounds

findings.current: The belt around So Gyo’s slender waist unfurled—no, it was a flexible sword.
findings.defect: “Unfurled” adds a specific motion that the Korean does not describe.
findings.rationale: The source identifies the object as a flexible sword and says it was aimed at him; it does not say the belt unfurled.
findings.replacement: The belt around So Gyo’s slender waist—no, a flexible sword—was filled with powerful internal energy and pointed at me.

findings.defect: “Elusive” suggests difficulty catching or understanding her, rather than the light, ethereal quality of the source description.
findings.rationale: The Korean “표횰하면서도 우아하다” describes her movement as ethereal and graceful; “elusive” changes that physical impression.

summary: The chapter is largely faithful, but a few phrases add or lose source-specific meaning and imagery.
